name: Unchained Monk Iron-Skinned Unchained Monk
body:
There is an innumerable amount of martial arts styles employed all over the world, but none focus on sheer bodily fortitude, armored combat, and usage of gauntlets and cestus like the iron-skinned style.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

At 1st level, an iron-skinned monk gains proficiency with the gauntlet, spiked gauntlet, cestus, and armor spikes.

Additionally, the iron-skinned monk gains proficiency in light armor.

This alters the unchained monk’s weapon and armor proficiencies.

Iron Skinned Style (Ex)

An iron-skinned monk uses their unarmed damage progression instead of the normal damage for cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets, and armor spikes and they may make their flurry of blows or stunning fist attacks with these weapons. All abilities of the unchained monk function while they are wearing light or no armor but still not while they are carrying a medium or heavy load.

This ability replaces the bonus feat normally gained at 1st level and an iron-skinned striker does not add their Wisdom bonus to their AC, though they still gain an improved AC bonus at 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter even while wearing light armor.

Ki Like Iron (Su)

When the iron-skinned monk gains a ki pool (at 3rd level for the unchained monk) they gain a new use for that ability.

When making a combat maneuver check the iron skinned monk may expend a point of ki to avoid an attack of opportunity from their target and adds their Wisdom bonus (minimum 1) to the combat maneuver check.

Beginning at 7th level, cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets, and armor spikes carried by the iron-skinned monk also benefits from ki strike.

This ability modifies ki strike.

Ever Vigilant (Ex)

At 5th level, all squares the iron-skinned monk threatens with a melee weapon or unarmed strike, are considered difficult terrain for enemies. This ability applies even to jumping, flying, and incorporeal foes, as well as swarms, so long as the iron-skinned monk wields a melee weapon or unarmed strike capable of affecting them. The iron-skinned monk must be aware of the enemy to affect them.

The iron-skinned monk also provides cover but not total cover to adjacent allies if their square lies between the ally and the origin of the attack or effect that includes the ally as a target.

This ability replaces purity of body.

Bulwark (Ex)

At 10th level, the iron-skinned monk has learned to defend against some kinds of magic. If they are wearing gauntlets or cestus they may expend a point of ki and deflect a ray effect that targets them as an immediate action causing it to harmlessly dissipate.

If the iron-skinned monk expends an additional point of ki they make a Reflex save against that ray using whatever the save DC vs the effect would normally be, even if it does not allow one. If they succeed they may redirect the ray to a target of their choice. The target must be within range of the spell as though the ironskinned monk was the point of origin. This redirection uses the same attack roll result by the original caster.

This ability replaces improved evasion.

Steel Reserves (Ex)

Beginning at 10th level, the ironskinned monk gains 2 bonus temporary ki at the beginning of each combat. This ki is used first before their normal pool of ki and if this bonus ki remains at the end of combat, it is lost.

This ability replaces the bonus feat normally gained at 10th level.

Steel Skinned Master (Ex/Su)

Beginning at 16th level for the unchained monk, the iron-skinned monk treats cestus, gauntlets, spiked gauntlets and armor spikes as though they were one size larger for the purpose of their unarmed damage progression. Furthermore they may spend a ki point to emulate the effects of stoneskin on themselves as a standard action using their character level as the caster level, while under the effects of this stoneskin effect they are also not subject to critical hits or precision damage.

This ability replaces the ki power gained at 16th level for the unchained monk.

Unyielding Iron

Beginning at 19th level, while the iron-skinned monk still has at least one point of ki in their pool they cannot be moved from their square by the force of another creature, spell, spell-like, or supernatural ability, or by other means. Natural forces such as gravity still affect the iron-skinned monk, though a tidal wave, gust of wind, or other such phenomenon may not as long as the iron-skinned monk is standing on a surface which can support their weight.

This ability replaces flawless mind for the unchained monk.
